subject: PII dataflow & access carveout — SLA exception plan
messages:
From: Jake Hollis <jake.hollis@medforma.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medforma.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary access carveout for ingestion SLA

Marissa —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We are reviewing the DPA and the onboarding SOW with procurement; there's one item blocking signature for the health data ingest pilot:

- Our operations team needs a guaranteed ingest SLA for certain PII event windows tied to clinical workflows. MedForma is asking for a carveout in the DPA to allow short-term access by a small set of Redwood engineers to a scoped subset of PII telemetry while we validate transforms and retention automation.

We know this is sensitive and want to be explicit about scope: the carveout would be time-boxed to 30 days, limited to records for the pilot tenant (tenant-id MF-PILOT-01), and require KMS-wrapped access, session recording, and additional audit exports.

Can you point me to the team who handles temporary exceptions? Also attaching the SLA request template we use for legal review.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a call.

—Jake
Jake Hollis
Head of Integrations | MedForma Health

Subject: Re: Request: temporary access carveout for ingestion SLA

Connor / Karthik / Neha —

Looping you in: MedForma has asked for a 30-day, tenant-scoped carveout that would allow a small set of our engineers to access (read-only) the pilot tenant PII records to validate transforms and retention hooks before we flip the pipeline to production. Requirements they listed: KMS access, session recording, audit export, and an SLA for ingest windows.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Connor: can you draft the scoped access runbook and list of exact roles/accounts that would need access? Start with least privilege (one service account + two engineers).
- Karthik: assess whether this carveout triggers any DPA changes or an annex; if so, what language is minimally required and what approvals we need from legal/security?
- Neha: what audit/log exports will we need to provide to MedForma to satisfy their ops team?

I attached an initial dataflow diagram (dataflow_v2.drawio.png) they shared in the onboarding packet. I tried to annotate the ingress points where engineers would need to validate PII normalization.

Let's aim for a reply to Jake by Thursday COB with a proposed control set and a short canary plan (how we validate and revoke access). If anyone needs a quick sync I'll set up 30m.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Customer Onboarding | Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Hollis <jake.hollis@medforma.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary access carveout for ingestion SLA

Marissa / team —

Quick notes from an infra/runbook perspective: putting together a minimal, auditable plan that supports the ask without broadening blast radius. Proposed controls:

1) Scoped environment: deploy a tenant-specific validation workspace (MF-PILOT-01-VAL) that mirrors the pipeline but contains only pilot records. Ingestion will route to validation namespace via a toggle.
2) Access model: one short-lived service account (svc-medforma-val) + two named engineer accounts. All accounts require MFA + conditional access (IP allowlist limited to our office + secops jumpbox).
3) KMS: use customer-created KMS key; access requests require an HSM policy change with two approvers (one from Redwood secops, one from MedForma).
4) Session recording & audit: stream session recordings to an immutable bucket, include keystroke-level logs for any console work, and emit an audit export every 6 hours.
5) Timebox & revoke: 30-day limit with automated revoke workflow (Job: revoke-access-mf-pilot-01 on day 31).
6) Canary validation: do a 72-hour dry-run with synthetic records to confirm transforms before allowing any access to real PII.

I can produce a short runbook (2-3 pages) and the Terraform snippets to create the workspace. The pieces that will need legal/security sign-off: KMS cross-access and the HSM approval flow.

If that sounds good I'll draft the runbook and a checklist for Marissa to send to MedForma.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Infrastructure Lead, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Hollis <jake.hollis@medforma.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medforma.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary access carveout for ingestion SLA

Marissa / Jake / all —

Legal/security review summary and next steps. Short answer: we can support a narrow carveout without changing the core DPA if we add a short annex and a signed exception form (SLA Exception Addendum). Conditions I recommend including in the addendum:

- Scope: explicit tenant-id (MF-PILOT-01) and resource ARNs; read-only access only to the validation workspace; no export rights.
- Duration: 30 calendar days from activation; automatic revoke at expiry.
- KMS: MedForma must supply a customer-managed KMS key; any decryption operations require a two-approver HSM policy change (Redwood secops + MedForma security lead).
- Logging & evidence: session recordings, audit exports every 6 hours, and a weekly digest delivered to MedForma with a curated redaction summary.
- Personnel: list of named engineers to be granted access; background checks or employment attestations optional but recommended for very sensitive workloads.
- Liability & indemnity: no additional changes to indemnity beyond standard DPA; MedForma must acknowledge the temporary nature and accept operational risk during the validation window.

I'll attach a one-page SLA Exception Addendum template to this thread. Connor — please add the runbook as an appendix and confirm the automated revoke job name. Marissa — once we have the engineer list from MedForma and their KMS ARN, legal can sign the addendum and we can schedule the 72-hour synthetic canary.

Jake / Elena — please let us know the engineers you expect to involve and confirm the KMS key details. If you prefer, we can run a 30m call tomorrow morning to finalize.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
attachments: SLA_Exception_Addendum_template.pdf (application/pdf)
